title: fix(gateway): interrupt worker teardown during shutdown
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown waiting minutes for a worker-environment teardown during reconciliation, until the service supervisor kills the process.

## User Impact

Shutdown can interrupt Crabbox capture, stop, and checkpoint cleanup, retain their durable recovery state, and retry the same cleanup after restart. Pending replies, terminal persistence, and actual child-process settlement keep their existing drain obligations. There is no schema, configuration, or retention change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observed pending operation was provider `destroy`, not inspection. Production traces showed it still pending after 219 seconds; another timeout had no active turns or pending owners. Both the earlier inspection cancellation fix (#180841) and cleanup-acceptance change (#182138) were already in the affected build. Crabbox's bounded stop budget is 16 minutes 45 seconds, but reconciliation dropped cancellation before reaching it.

The teardown owner now supplies Gateway lifecycle cancellation for normal, failed-bootstrap, and expired-preparation cleanup, and Crabbox forwards it through its command chain. Explicit turn cancellation still runs compensating cleanup; it does not cancel teardown. The existing provider deadline also aborts destroy. The owner still joins the underlying mutation; a timeout or cancellation does not falsely declare physical teardown complete. The additive optional `destroy.signal` provider contract documents that requirement.

## Evidence

- Core shutdown and provider-timeout regressions fail on unchanged main because destroy receives no cancellation signal. Candidate tests verify interruption, retained identity, reopening the store, and cleanup retry after restart; failed-bootstrap cleanup preserves the original failure.
- Crabbox real-child regressions cover capture, stop, and post-stop checkpoint deletion. Interrupted deletion retains retirement debt, and normal provider maintenance clears it later. All 46 tests in the three focused plugin files pass.
- Existing preserve-only drain and real Gateway-close persistence tests pass. Focused reconciliation/allocation proof: 32/32; provisioning, node provisioning, explicit-cancellation, and lifecycle siblings also exercised. Targeted core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export collision guard, and 22 closure tests pass. PR CI supplies broad validation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): addressed cancellation gaps in bootstrap-failure cleanup and post-stop checkpoint retirement; final review clean.

Acceptance declared before the process/load measurements: the real isolated dist Gateway must interrupt a hanging fixture destroy and exit cleanly within a 20-second budget, retain the exact lease, and complete cleanup after restart. Base must reproduce the blocked shutdown. Required Team-shaped load comparison uses the canonical harness, 10-minute arms, two counterbalanced timing and allocation pairs. Report server-side latency and host load, and obtain A/A controls before treating an adverse load metric as a regression.

Runtime code delta: +32 net lines for lifecycle cancellation, the existing deadline abort, and the additive provider contract. No second lifecycle owner or state store was introduced. The separate 340-line script is reproducible process proof.

Real dist-Gateway reproduction passed on base `9db139fcf842` versus candidate `5c33ee10cc36`: baseline remained blocked at the 20,002.5 ms harness deadline and required SIGKILL; candidate aborted provider teardown and exited cleanly in 801.7 ms. Candidate retained the exact lease and operation ID with a visible interruption, and the next boot completed cleanup. Clean shutdown after replay was 640.7 ms on base and 591.0 ms on candidate. This is isolated synthetic process evidence, not a live deployment timing claim.

Both full builds passed; all 281 shared compiled package files are byte-identical between builds. The initial stress attempt failed during setup because the instrumentation loader disabled source aliases but could not resolve two worker-telemetry workspace dependencies. The loader now resolves those dependencies through the measured build’s compiled exports while leaving built-runtime imports untouched. Its real-child regression fails on the original loader; all six focused harness tests and a native-subagent smoke pass, with independent review clean. No performance verdict is drawn from failed setup or smoke runs. The full canonical stress campaign below completed successfully on the same final head.


## Completed load acceptance

Canonical harness from this tooling head: two AB/BA pairs for untraced timing and two separate AB/BA allocation pairs, eight fresh 10-minute measurement windows plus warmup. Each arm used 10,800 synthetic sessions, 40 enabled bundled plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, four concurrent mock-provider turns per round, real tool calls/native subagents, and list/search/history/sidebar churn. All eight arms passed workload coverage and error checks; each completed 40 reported parent turns and matching tool results. Only isolated loopback development Gateways were exercised.

Mean across the two matched pairs (percentage column is the mean of the two paired percentage deltas):

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Absolute delta | Paired relative delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Main-thread CPU % | 7.449 | 7.826 | +0.377 | +5.13% |
| Allocation MiB/s | 27.719 | 28.100 | +0.381 | +1.38% |
| GC s/min | 0.143 | 0.157 | +0.014 | +9.68% |
| Loop p99 ms | 30.859 | 31.597 | +0.737 | +2.46% |
| Client list p99 ms | 41.937 | 45.394 | +3.456 | +8.21% |
| Handler mean ms | 11.138 | 11.988 | +0.850 | +7.69% |
| Handler p99 estimate ms | 35.394 | 38.691 | +3.297 | +9.31% |
| RSS MiB | 2649.176 | 2637.296 | -11.880 | -0.45% |
| Main heap MiB | 653.174 | 700.080 | +46.907 | +7.19% |

These steady-state differences do not cross the predeclared adverse gates. Total untraced GC rose by 14 ms/min, below the 50 ms/min materiality floor; no maximum GC pause exceeded 50 ms or twice its paired baseline. This is a shutdown/recovery improvement, not a steady-state throughput claim. No A/A rejection investigation was triggered; the small differences are not attributed causally to this patch.

Each host-load window has 20–21 samples on a 32-logical-CPU Mac; no window was excluded after observing results. Achieved list/RPC rates and full workload completion were checked, rather than assuming offered load equals completed work.

Handler values use first-to-last scrape counter deltas, excluding warmup and omitting up to the final 15 seconds. Handler p99 is a histogram bucket estimate, not exact client latency. Each timing handler p99 falls in the 30–40 ms bucket and has 1,173 observations; client list tails have 1,202–1,204 samples and loop tails approximately 28,000. Major-GC per-collection percentiles are context only because each timing arm has fewer than 50 collections.

## Final validation

Exact head `5c33ee10cc3674437aaa4762930b811f897ce15c`: [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40193391020), [build passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40193390710), no reruns. Independent local review, GitHub Codex review, and ClawSweeper identified no remaining actionable findings. ClawSweeper's previously unfinished load-evidence item is completed above.

Remaining limits: the historical trace identifies provider `destroy`, not which individual Crabbox child command was pending. Tests cover all three command boundaries. Third-party providers must honor the optional signal; the owner intentionally keeps waiting for actual mutation settlement rather than falsely releasing a live write. No production restart or live deployment timing is claimed.
